# The whole dependency tree every GitHub job installs, pinned exactly (2026-10-24).
# requirements.txt names eight packages; their own dependencies (streamlit's pyarrow, altair, protobuf, tornado;
# plotly's narwhals; pandas' python-dateutil) were resolved afresh on every run, so the jobs ran on whatever was
# newest that day. Measured: python-dateutil 2.9.0.post0 until 21 Oct 2026, then 3.0.0 (a major release three days
# old, newer than pandas 2.3.3 itself) from 22 Oct.
# This is the set pip installed on ubuntu-24.04 / Python 3.13 in run 39617674220 (21 Oct 2026), which published that
# day's v2 lists: the last set before the drift. A back-fill rebuilt 21-23 Oct byte for byte with the drifted set (run
# 40094645819); the commit that pinned this set records its own compare. Every install passes it with -c
# (tests/test_ci_constraints.py). Every requirement, on main AND at both pinned code commits (FEED_CODE_SHA,
# V2_CODE_SHA), equals its line here: while a pin names a version, a bump on main cannot be made here (pip would
# refuse both pinned jobs). Refresh this set only with a back-fill compare. ASCII only: pip reads it on a Linux box.
